title: AI-assisted Hubble asteroid sample extends the shallow size-distribution slope to H≈20
summary: Using 632 serendipitously imaged Hubble Space Telescope asteroids found by the prior AI-assisted Hubble Asteroid Hunter survey, the authors fit trail parallax to estimate distances, absolute magnitudes, and approximate sizes. Their cumulative magnitude distribution has a shallower slope (α≈0.26) from H=15 to about H=20, extending the previously reported trend by roughly two magnitudes; the analyzed sample is dominated by potential main-belt objects smaller than 1 km.
ai_technology: Google Cloud deep-learning asteroid-trail detector trained on Hubble Asteroid Hunter citizen-science classifications (upstream survey)
organization: European Space Agency; European Space Astronomy Centre; Autonomous University of Madrid; Astronomical Institute of the Romanian Academy; University of Craiova; Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Université Côte d’Azur

evidence.tested: Using 632 serendipitously imaged Hubble Space Telescope asteroids found by the prior AI-assisted Hubble Asteroid Hunter survey, the authors fit trail parallax to estimate distances, absolute magnitudes, and approximate sizes.
evidence.unknown: The 632-object sample comprises 454 unmatched and 178 known objects; unmatched does not mean every object is independently confirmed or has a reliable orbit. Only about 40% of raw objects yielded meaningful distance estimates after filtering. Sizes assume spherical objects and a uniform albedo of 0.15. The authors state that the combined archive sample is not a dedicated or observationally unbiased survey, and the result is an extension of the size-distribution slope to H≈20 rather than a complete census.
evidence.ai_role: The primary study states that the input asteroid trails were detected in the preceding Hubble Asteroid Hunter work using a deep-learning algorithm trained on volunteer classifications. This AI-assisted search supplied the previously unidentified trail sample; the present paper then applies a parallax-fitting method and magnitude-distribution analysis to characterize it. The quantitative population result depends on this archive-scale AI-assisted detection pipeline and the present physical analysis.
